headline: The U.S. Air Force has moved forward with production of two unmanned fighter aircraft under its Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) program, rather than selecting a single design. Contracts have gone to General Atomics for the FQ-42A Dark Merlin and Anduril for the FQ-44A Fury. Both platforms had previously been tested under the YFQ-42A and YFQ-44A designations. The aircraft are intended to act as semi-autonomous wingmen alongside crewed fighters, helping increase combat mass without requiring a proportional rise in the number of pilots or traditional jets. The approach is meant to spread risk and divide roles across multiple systems instead of relying on a single type of aircraft. Rather than one universal unmanned combat aerial vehicle (UCAV), the Air Force is effectively building a mixed fleet, with each design offering different strengths that can be developed further over time. In the near term, the goal is to field more than 150 of these combat-capable wingmen by the end of the decade, with early units used mainly for testing, validation, and gradual operational integration.

headline: Iranian F-5 pilots recounted the March 1 airstrikes on the U.S. Camp Buehring in Kuwait. According to their account, they were aware of the presence of Patriot batteries, layered air defenses, AWACS coverage, and Kuwaiti F/A-18s. To avoid detection, they maintained complete radio silence and flew at extremely low altitude over the Gulf, less than 50 feet above the water, far below the standard 500-foot training profile. One pilot claimed the aircraft even passed between two ships whose decks stood higher than the jet itself. After entering Kuwaiti airspace, they bypassed other potential targets, including power lines and refineries, and proceeded directly toward Camp Buehring, maintaining high speed and very low altitude until reaching the target area. The pilots stated that the strike caused major fires and multiple secondary explosions, including burning helicopters.
